POST /v1/refunds HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer mk_live_...
Idempotency-Key: rf_3b8d1c4e-... { "charge_id": "ch_01HWX9ABC...", "amount_minor": 4999, "reason": "requested_by_customer"
}

steps.title: API validates and claims refund idempotency
steps.action: Refund has its own idempotency key space. The API also verifies that charge_id exists and is in captured status before dispatching.
steps.codeOrCommand:
claimed = redis.set(f"idem:{merchant_id}:{refund_idem_key}", '{"status":"in_flight"}', nx=True, ex=86400)
assert claimed, "retry collapsed — replay cached response"
charge = ledger.get_charge(body.charge_id)
assert charge.status == 'captured', "can only refund captured charges"
assert body.amount_minor <= charge.amount_minor, "refund cannot exceed capture"

steps.title: Refund idempotency key claimed
steps.codeOrCommand: SET idem:mk_acct_42:rf_3b8d1c4e-... '{"status":"in_flight"}' NX EX 86400

steps.title: Orchestrator allocates refund_id and persists pending refund
steps.action: Same saga pattern — durable intent row before external call.
steps.codeOrCommand:
refund_id = f"rf_{ulid.new}"
ledger.execute(""" INSERT INTO refunds (id, charge_id, amount_minor, currency, status, created_at) VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, 'pending', now)
""", (refund_id, charge_id, 4999, 'USD'))

steps.title: Pending refund row persisted
Orchestrator calls Stripe refund API
steps.action: Refund against the ORIGINAL stripe charge id, with our refund_id as idempotency key.
steps.codeOrCommand:
POST https://api.stripe.com/v1/refunds
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...
Idempotency-Key: rf_01HWXA... charge=ch_3OaStripeGeneratedId&amount=4999 # Stripe response
{ "id": "re_3PaStripeRefundId", "status": "succeeded", "amount": 4999, "charge": "ch_3OaStripeGeneratedId"
}

steps.title: Compensating double-entry written
steps.action: Refund is the mirror of the charge: credit the customer (we owe them their money back), debit the merchant balance. Same single-transaction atomicity.
steps.codeOrCommand:
BEGIN; UPDATE refunds
SET status = 'succeeded', psp_refund_id = 're_3PaStripeRefundId'
WHERE id = 'rf_01HWXA...'; UPDATE charges
SET status = 'refunded'
WHERE id = 'ch_01HWX9ABC...'; -- Credit customer (giving money back)
INSERT INTO ledger_entries (charge_id, account_id, direction, amount_minor, currency, posted_at)
VALUES ('ch_01HWX9ABC...', 'customer_card:tok_visa_4242', 'C', 4999, 'USD', now); -- Debit merchant balance
INSERT INTO ledger_entries (charge_id, account_id, direction, amount_minor, currency, posted_at)
VALUES ('ch_01HWX9ABC...', 'merchant_balance:mk_acct_42', 'D', 4999, 'USD', now); COMMIT;

steps.title: Merchant balance decremented
Emits RefundSucceeded event (fire-and-forget)
steps.codeOrCommand:
kafka.produce( topic="payments.events", value={ "type": "refund.succeeded", "refund_id": "rf_01HWXA...", "charge_id": "ch_01HWX9ABC...", "amount_minor": 4999 }
)

steps.title: Refund idempotency key updated with response
steps.codeOrCommand:
redis.set( f"idem:mk_acct_42:rf_3b8d1c4e-...", json.dumps({"status":"done", "http_status":201, "body":{...}}), ex=86400
)

steps.title: API returns 201 with the refund
steps.codeOrCommand:
return Response(status=201, body={ "refund_id": "rf_01HWXA...", "charge_id": "ch_01HWX9ABC...", "status": "succeeded", "amount_minor": 4999, "currency": "USD"
})

operations.title: Reconciliation sweep (daily batch)
operations.name: Reconciliation sweep (daily batch)
operations.description: Nightly job pulls the PSP settlement file and diffs it against the ledger. Any mismatch pages on-call.

steps.title: Job starts at 02:00 local — fetches Stripe settlement report
steps.action: A scheduled worker kicks off the reconciliation job. First step is to pull the PSP's settlement file for the previous 24h close.
steps.codeOrCommand:
# 02:00 cron
report = stripe.reports.retrieve( type='balance.summary', interval_start=yesterday_00_00_utc, interval_end=today_00_00_utc
)
rows = csv_download(report.file_url) # ~1M rows

steps.title: Ledger scan: all captured/refunded charges in the window
steps.action: Large read served by a read replica to avoid impacting the live write path.

steps.title: Diff: PSP rows ↔ ledger rows by psp_charge_id
steps.action: Build two in-memory maps keyed by psp_charge_id. Walk both sides; record any mismatch into a discrepancies table.
steps.codeOrCommand:
psp_map = { r['charge_id']: r for r in psp_rows }
local_map = { r['psp_charge_id']: r for r in local_rows } discrepancies = for psp_id, psp_row in psp_map.items: local = local_map.get(psp_id) if local is None: discrepancies.append({"kind":"orphan_psp_charge", "psp_id": psp_id}) elif local['amount_minor']!= psp_row['amount_minor']: discrepancies.append({"kind":"amount_mismatch", "psp_id": psp_id, "local": local['amount_minor'], "psp": psp_row['amount_minor']}) for psp_id, local in local_map.items: if psp_id not in psp_map: discrepancies.append({"kind":"missing_from_settlement", "psp_id": psp_id})

steps.title: Write discrepancies for audit
Pages on-call via PagerDuty (fire-and-forget)
steps.action: Any non-zero discrepancy count pages on-call. Zero discrepancies is the steady state — even 3 rows out of 1M is worth investigating.
steps.codeOrCommand:
kafka.produce( topic="ops.alerts", value={ "severity": "P2", "service": "payments", "title": "Reconciliation discrepancies detected", "run_id": "recon_2026_04_24", "count": 3, "breakdown": {"amount_mismatch": 1, "missing_from_settlement": 2} }
)
steps.note: Never self-heal automatically — reconciliation drift often means a code bug or PSP anomaly. A human must triage before the ledger is touched.

tradeoffs.decision: Client-supplied idempotency keys vs server-generated dedupe
tradeoffs.chosen: Client generates a UUIDv4 per checkout attempt; server stores it in Redis with SETNX
tradeoffs.rationale: Only the client knows which retries belong to the same logical intent. Server-side fuzzy dedupe on (amount, card, time window) produces false positives for legitimate repeat purchases (e.g., two coffees in a row). The tradeoff is that buggy clients can defeat dedupe by rotating keys — we mitigate with a server-side alert on duplicate (merchant, card, amount) within 60s.

tradeoffs.decision: Strong consistency vs availability on the write path
tradeoffs.chosen: Strong consistency — single Postgres primary per region with synchronous replicas
tradeoffs.rationale: Money requires a linearizable ledger; CP beats AP here. During a primary failover the charge API returns 503 for a few seconds rather than accept writes that could diverge. We accept the availability hit because a 30s outage is recoverable, whereas a split-brain ledger is not.

tradeoffs.decision: Synchronous PSP call vs async queue-based capture
tradeoffs.chosen: Synchronous with tight timeouts (30s hard cap), retries only on idempotent operations
tradeoffs.rationale: Customers expect an immediate pass/fail at checkout, so async-only breaks UX. Async does work for later operations (refunds, payouts) where users don't block on a response. The cost of sync is that PSP latency is on our critical path — we mitigate with per-PSP circuit breakers and a fallback PSP for resilient merchants.

tradeoffs.decision: Single ledger table vs per-tenant sharding
tradeoffs.chosen: One logical ledger, time-partitioned by charge_date; shard only if a single tenant dominates volume
tradeoffs.rationale: At 1M charges/day the entire 7-year ledger fits in ~1.1TB — one well-tuned Postgres cluster handles it. Sharding adds cross-shard txn complexity (money movements between tenants) we don't need yet. The tradeoff is that hot merchants on Black Friday can create contention; partition pruning plus read replicas cover it until a tenant needs its own shard.

tradeoffs.decision: Webhook processing: inline handler vs Kafka-buffered consumer
tradeoffs.chosen: Inline handler writes to a webhook_events table keyed by event_id, then processes
tradeoffs.rationale: PSPs deliver webhooks at-least-once, so we need an event_id dedupe store anyway. Adding Kafka is pure complexity unless we need consumer-side fanout (notification, analytics, fraud). We punt Kafka to phase 2 when more consumers show up.

interviewFollowUps.question: Multi-PSP routing: fall over to a secondary PSP when the primary breaches a latency or error budget
3DS / SCA flow for European PSD2 compliance — interactive authentication before capture
Push ledger events to a data warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery) via CDC for finance reporting
Chargeback and dispute workflow with evidence upload to the PSP
Currency conversion and multi-currency ledger accounts with FX-rate lock at charge time
Fraud scoring pre-authorization (Sift, Forter) with a decline-or-review decision on high-risk charges
